subject.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated

question: Should Doctor treat an exposed Gateway as authenticated—and replace token-remediation critical guidance with a trusted-proxy warning—only when the PR’s stricter host-scoped proxy and explicit-origin readiness checks succeed?
rationale: The patch does not modify runtime authorization, but it changes the security meaning and remediation shown to operators for an exposed Gateway. That threshold is a product security policy decision that tests alone cannot select.

options.title: Approve the fail-closed diagnostic policy
options.body: Accept the host-scoped proxy, runtime authorization, and explicit-origin prerequisites, then refresh the branch against current main before merge.

options.title: Retain the current critical classification
options.body: Keep trusted-proxy deployments on the unauthenticated critical path until a broader owner-approved Doctor security policy is designed.

options.title: Choose a different documented threshold
options.body: Specify which runtime-accepted trusted-proxy configurations Doctor should recognize, then request a focused revision and tests for that policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the fail-closed diagnostic policy
recommendation.body: Accept the host-scoped proxy, runtime authorization, and explicit-origin prerequisites, then refresh the branch against current main before merge.
